name: Hollis Fenn
role: Mooring-warden and bell of Keel Town
bio: Keel Town grew off the Mesa's west rim one hung hull at a time, and Hollis Fenn has rung it together ever since: mooring-warden of the slung town, keeper of the bell code, and the only official the hang-tenants elected twice (once by acclamation, once by accident during a storm vote that nobody called). Devanna Shore holds the Guild's masts topside; Hollis holds everything that dangles beneath them — which, as he explains to inspectors, is a separate jurisdiction with its own wind. He pays couriers out of a tin marked MOORAGE, does not ask what hums inside a sealed crate, and considers a favour banked better than money.
appearance: A sun-hollowed man in his fifties with a bell-rope shoulder, storm-battered Guild vest turned inside out so only the stitching shows, brass ring-keys on a length of ship's line, one boot re-soled with winch leather, and a speaking-trumpet slung crosswise on his back like a cutlass.
voice: Ship's-bell cadence — his sentences strike. Declares things like weather observations that happen to be threats or kindnesses. Smuggler's discretion: he never heard nothing, but he did overhear a great deal. Calls couriers 'young tonnage'. His warmth is real and his accounting is warmer.

greetings: Strikes three of the afternoon, and here comes young tonnage. Keel Town's open to whoever ties on polite.
Varga. The west cleat held all winter and I am not taking questions about it. What's the sky sent us?
Mind the drop between docks four and five — she only bites riders who flatter the height.
barks: The bell says what I say. Convenient arrangement. Ask the hang-tenants; they'll confirm the bell is honest.
Devanna runs what you can stand on. I run what you can't. Jurisdiction, young tonnage, is mostly about where gravity files complaints.
If that crate hums, keep humming along. Ships sound better with accompaniment.
A favour held is worth two favours spent and one never mentioned. That's Keel Town arithmetic and it audits.
mission: The Guild's offer wax goes up to the mesa house and the *interesting* wax comes to me. Guess which kind this is. Deliver like you never noticed the difference.
Keel Town Quarterly, young tonnage — every hull gets one, even the hull that swears it's a raft. Drop, bell, next. Last courier tried to read a copy in flight and the magazine won.
Somebody left moorage pay on the night ring again without a name. Third season running. Do not investigate. Investigate nothing at speed.
radio: Keel Town band. Bell's rung for weather from the spine — hang your speed, young tonnage, the rim gusts mean it today.
Hollis on the hang-band. If anybody asks, your hold is empty, your route is dull, and I've never seen you. If nobody asks: welcome back, there's soup.
Traffic note: the mesa house wants a word about a crate nobody entered. Come by the west approach. The west approach has terrible record-keeping.
The slung hulls are singing in the wind tonight. G chord, mostly rust. I'll ring it down at dusk — somebody should.
night: Night mooring, young tonnage: ring twice, wait for the lamp, tie off on the honest cleat. The dishonest one has a view of the drop you'll remember.
After dark, Keel Town answers to the bell and the bell answers to me, and I — at my age — answer to whoever brings tea. Constitution's on a plate of tin under dock three. Very moving.
